subject: Transit credits, KV-cache risk, and fallback packaging — EchoHealth
messages:
From: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@echohealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify transit credit split and KV-cache persistence question

Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks for the package you sent over this morning. A couple of clarifying questions before we take this to procurement:

- Can you break out the proposed $120k introductory credit into prepay vs runtime credits? We need visibility into how much is applied up-front vs offsetting usage over Q1.
- Our platform team is concerned about KV-cache (prefix) persistence during the migration window. If the cache needs to be rebuilt from cold, we could see a meaningful cost/latency spike in the first 48 hours. What guarantees or operational support do you offer to mitigate that?

Other asks: please include a short ops fallback plan and an explicit SLA carveout (if any) for the switchover period. Procurement will also want a single SOW with the credit language inline.

Can you respond with a redline of the credit split and a short technical note on the KV-cache warmup strategy?

Appreciate it — we’re trying to get this signed before the end of the quarter.

Olivia Harper
Head of Platform Partnerships
EchoHealth

Subject: Re: Clarify transit credit split and KV-cache persistence question

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear call-outs. Quick answers and a proposed split below, plus attached artifacts (credits workbook + updated SOW draft).

1) Credit split (proposed):
   - $50,000 one-time onboarding/prepay credit (applies at contract execution to professional services and one-time onboarding fees)
   - $70,000 usage credit applied as token-usage offsets across Q1 (applied monthly until exhausted; visible on monthly invoices)

   Rationale: prepay covers the upfront hands-on migration and runbook validation; the usage credits reduce your early production unit cost while you ramp.

2) KV-cache (prefix) warmup and ops support:
   - We will provide a two-day assisted warmup run: Redwood engineers (Soojin) + EchoHealth infra will execute scripted traffic replay to prefill the KV cache.
   - Fallback policy: automatic fallback to a lower-cost, high-availability model variant for the initial 72-hour window if latency exceeds the SLOs.
   - Monitoring: we’ll instrument token-level latency and cache-hit dashboards and provide a 24/7 on-call handover during the first 96 hours.

3) SLA carveout:
   - Normal SLA applies except for a 72-hour migration window during which the target p50/p95 are best-effort with credits available if persistent breaches (>6 hours) occur (we’ll include explicit credit language in the SOW).

Next steps: attached updated SOW (EchoHealth-SOW-v3.pdf) with credit clause inserted and an XLSX that breaks the credits into line items (redwood-credits-breakdown.xlsx). Ben has also summarized the warmup steps below for your infra team.

If this looks good I can push the SOW to DocuSign and we’ll mark the credits in the HubSpot deal record.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Subject: KV-cache warmup technical note (brief)

Olivia / Kimberly — quick technical note attached and inline summary: kv-warmup-note.txt attached.

Summary:
- Replay size: our recommendation is a 48-hour replay window derived from a rolling 7-day sample (we’ll sample the 48 hours that best represent peak QPS for cold-start coverage).
- Tooling: Redwood will provide a containerized replay utility that consumes sanitized logs (we can run it in your VPC or ship a set of precomputed payloads if EchoHealth prefers no external tooling).
- Telemetry: we’ll collect cache-hit rate, per-shard latency, token-level p50/p95, and a small set of anonymized request hashes to validate hit-mapping. We will not persist PII or request bodies beyond the warmup run.
- Fallback behavior: if cache-hit < 10% after 24 hours we’ll trigger a staged canary that routes 10% traffic to the warmed cluster and provide a rollback script to route back to the old vendor without session loss.

I’ll be on the warmup call if you want to go over the sequence.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Olivia / EchoHealth procurement team — following the thread and Ben’s note, here’s the consolidated proposal we’ll push to DocuSign:

- Credit schedule (inlined in SOW):
  • $50,000 onboarding credit (applied at signature to professional services).
  • $70,000 runtime credit applied monthly across Q1 until exhausted (line items enumerated by invoice month).

- Warmup and fallback ops (in SOW):
  • Redwood provides containerized replay tooling; option to run in EchoHealth VPC for security.
  • 48-hour replay window based on a rolling sample; Redwood collects cache-hit rate, per-shard latency, and anonymized request hashes only during run.
  • 72-hour migration window with best-effort SLA; if breaches >6 hours we’ll apply service credits per the SOW formula.
  • Fallback: staged canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with an automated rollback script to route back to current vendor; fallback compute falls within the committed pool and does not consume additional credits (it runs within the reserved capacity).

Documents attached: EchoHealth-SOW-v3.pdf (SOW with the credit schedule inlined), redwood-credits-breakdown.xlsx (line-item credit allocation).

Thanks all — looking forward to getting EchoHealth live.
